text:
maria: Heads-up — since ~02:10 we've got a flurry of PodPending in eu-west-1-gpu: `0/18 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 6 node(s) had incompatible GPU topology`. Multiple services impacted (model-infer, ckpt-loader). Anyone digging in?

sam: saw it too. Dashboard shows lots of small inference pods already running but new ones won't fit. Looks like MIG-sliced nodes with leftover fragments.

jon: quick check — are pods requesting full GPUs? Our CSI/device-plugin reports MIG slices as individual devices but some pods ask for `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` while other long-lived jobs carved out 1g slices. Binpacking mismatch + exclusive scheduling = fragmentation.

maria: yes, model-infer deployments request `resources.requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and we have a mix of 40GB and 20GB GPUs partitioned into different MIG profiles. New pods need full GPU but free capacity is in 1g slices. :thinking_face:

infra-bot: Scheduler events (excerpt):
```
I0318 02:12:03.123456 1 scheduler_predicates.go:223] Pod model-infer-xyz: 0/18 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 6 Node(s) had incompatible GPU topology.
I0318 02:12:03.123789 1 scheduler_binder.go:78] Pod cannot be scheduled, waiting for scale-up (no matching node group for required instance type).
```

sam: note the second line — CA thinks there's no matching nodegroup. Our manifests set nodeSelector: `gpu.family: a100` for high-mem jobs; autoscaler groups only include mixed-a10g pools. So two problems: fragmentation + mismatched nodegroup labels.

elaine: ops: CA's scale-up blocked because `maxTotalNodes` reached on eu-west-1 and the policy forbids creating new instance-type groups. We're at commit size for reserved pools.

jon: short-term fixes:
- relax nodeSelector on non-critical replicas to allow placement on a10g pool
- reduce request->limit mismatch (some pods set limits>requests which confuses packing heuristics)
- consolidate small models onto a shared GPU-serving process to avoid many 1-GPU pods

maria: can we patch a rollout? I'll flip nodeSelector for model-infer to prefer, not require `gpu.family`, and add toleration/affinity to prefer a100 but allow a10g. Minimal change.

sam: also request we upgrade device-plugin to v0.10 — it had fixes for reporting MIG topology. That might reduce the "incompatible GPU topology" false-positives.

elaine: opened CLOUD-1428 to raise eu-west-1 autoscaler quota with infra accounting (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CLOUD-1428). Adding ops oncall.

jon: medium-term: create a small nodepool with 8xA100 (no MIG) reserved for large ckpt-loader jobs, and another pool with MIG-enabled A10g for dense small infer replicas. Improves packing and reduces fragmentation.

maria: do we have telemetry to show how many GPUs are fragmented vs fully free? Might help justify new pool.

infra-bot: Metric snapshot (02:15):
```
eu-west-1-gpu pool: total gpus=288, allocated full-gpus=184, allocated-MIG-slices=68 (equivalent full-gpus=17), free-fragments=19
fragmentation-index ~ 0.17 (estimated)
```

sam: that fragmentation-index is high for bursty workloads. Cost vs fragmentation tradeoff argument incoming.

elaine: action items: 1) maria to patch nodeSelector -> prefer (PR #4221), 2) sam to test device-plugin bump in staging, 3) jon to draft nodepool proposal and cost delta, 4) ops to request quota increase (CLOUD-1428).

maria: I'll push the patch now and start a small canary.

jon: one more tip: for model-infer replicas, consider using `topologySpreadConstraints` with `WhenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule` removed — that will give scheduler more freedom to pack.

maria: noted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

elaine: ping @oncall when changes go live so we can watch autoscaler logs for unintended scale-ups.

sam: will monitor. If we still see > 5 pods pending after 10m we'll revert.
